lessons.title: Séimhiú san aimsir chaite
lessons.rule: In the past tense, a verb that begins with a consonant takes séimhiú: add h after the first letter (glan becomes ghlan). With muid, just put muid after the lenited verb: bhuail muid.
steps: Find the root of the verb in brackets: glan.
Add h after the first letter: ghlan.
Put the verb first, then the rest of the sentence: Ghlan Cathal scáileán an táibléid.

lessons.title: Ceist a fhreagairt
lessons.en: Answering a question in the past
lessons.rule: To answer a question that starts with Ar, drop Ar, keep the lenited verb and change tú to mé (and do to mo, ort to orm): Ar ghlan tú? Ghlan mé.
steps: Drop Ar from the start of the question: chuir tú an pláta ar an tábla.
Keep the h on the verb and give it a capital: Chuir tú an pláta ar an tábla.
Change tú to mé: Chuir mé an pláta ar an tábla.

lessons.title: Briathra nach nglacann séimhiú
lessons.rule: A verb beginning with l, n, r, sc, sm, sp or st cannot take séimhiú, so in the past tense the root stays exactly as it is: las, rith, scuab, scríobh. This is true after Níor as well: Níor scuab sé. But s followed by a vowel, l, n or r does take h: sheas, shiúil, shnámh.
steps: Find the root of the verb in brackets: las.
Check the first letter: l cannot take h.
Leave the root as it is and put it first: Las Pádraig an scáileán ar a fhón.

example.prompt: (Las) Pádraig an scáileán ar a fhón.
example.answer: Las Pádraig an scáileán ar a fhón.

more.answer: Scuab Gráinne urlár an halla spóirt.

lessons.hint: l, n, r, sc, sm, sp and st: no h. S + vowel, l, n or r: h (sheas, shnámh).

lessons.title: D' roimh ghuta agus roimh f
lessons.en: d' before a vowel and before f
lessons.rule: If the verb begins with a vowel, put d' in front of it (ól becomes d'ól). If it begins with f, add the h and then d' (fág becomes d'fhág). After Níor or Ar the d' goes: Níor ól, Níor fhás.
steps: Find the root of the verb in brackets: fág.
It begins with f, so add h: fhág.
Put d' in front: d'fhág.
Put the verb first: D'fhág Ciarán a mhála scoile ar an bhus.

lessons.title: Ceist le Ar, diúltach le Níor
lessons.en: Questions with Ar, negatives with Níor
lessons.rule: To ask a question put Ar before the verb, and for a negative put Níor; both lenite a consonant, and a vowel or f verb loses its d': Ar ól tú? Ar fhan tú? If the answer uses mé, ask with tú; if it uses muid, ask with sibh.
steps: Start from the answer: D'fhág mé.
Drop the d' and put Ar in front, keeping the h: Ar fhág.
Change mé to tú and add the rest: Ar fhág tú an leabhar anseo?

example.answer: Ar fhág tú an leabhar anseo?

more.answer: Ar chuir sibh an pláta ar an tábla?

lessons.hint: Ar or Níor, then h on a consonant, and never d'.

lessons.title: An saorbhriathar: -adh
lessons.rule: When nobody is named as doing the action, add -adh to a broad root (last vowel a, o or u) and do not lenite it: díol becomes díoladh.
steps: Find the root of the verb in brackets: díol.
The last vowel is o, so the root is broad: add -adh to get díoladh.
Do not add h, and put it first: Díoladh na ticéid go léir ar líne.

lessons.title: An saorbhriathar: -eadh
lessons.rule: If the last vowel of the root is i or e (a slender root), add -eadh instead, still with no h: cuir becomes cuireadh, druid becomes druideadh.
steps: Find the root of the verb in brackets: bain.
The last vowel is i, so the root is slender: add -eadh to get baineadh.
Do not add h, and put it first: Baineadh an féar Dé Sathairn.

lessons.title: An saorbhriathar: gan d', gan séimhiú
lessons.en: The autonomous form: no d', no lenition
lessons.rule: The autonomous form never takes d' or h, even when the verb begins with a vowel or f, and even after Ar or Níor: óladh, fágadh, Ar díoladh?
steps: Find the root of the verb in brackets: úsáid.
The last vowel is i, so add -eadh: úsáideadh.
Do not put d' in front, and put it first: Úsáideadh an peann dearg sa scrúdú.

example.answer: Úsáideadh an peann dearg sa scrúdú.

lessons.hint: Autonomous form: no d', no h, ever.
